text:
Sara K: Heads up — noticed a customer with a VPC binding getting routed to public pool when they send X-Workspace: <workspace-id> + Host: app.redwood.test. Logs show workspace header winning over VPC lookup.

Dave: whoa. can you paste the raw request/route decision?

Sara K: snippet from gateway log: 
```
match: header(X-Workspace) -> scope=workspace:abc123
route: pool=shared-gcpu-1
vpc_check: not performed
```

mira: hmm our intended order was: token/vpc binding -> header hints -> fallback workspace. looks like a regression in the matcher prioritization.

ben: is this the header-based routing flag we shipped last month? maybe rule ordering got inverted during refactor.

Sara K: yep that flag. repro steps attached: customer repro via curl and gateway trace. They had private endpoint enabled but header forced a shared pool route.

Dave: immediate mitigation: enforce VPC/customer binding assert before any header-derived scope. i.e. if request originates from a private endpoint or token tied to a dedicated pool, short-circuit and ignore X-Workspace header.

mira: agreed. two implementation options:
- strict: drop header-derived routing entirely when vpc/dedicated binding present (safer)
- soft: prefer vpc binding but emit telemetry and an alert if header causes mismatch (allows backwards compat)

ben: prefer strict for security reasons. we can still add a console toggle for permissive mode for a few enterprise customers that relied on header hacks.

gateway-bot: deploy plan template created: https://internal.redwood/deploys/2055554321 (automated)

Sara K: rollout plan: patch in gateway matcher to check vpcBinding first, unit tests, staging canary 5% traffic for 24h, metric: misroute.rate (requests where workspace != bound workspace), console breadcrumb for any autopaths affected. rollback via feature-flag toggle.

Dave: don't forget to add an audit log entry when we ignore a header so customers have visibility. and update docs/console UX to show "Routing enforced by VPC binding" on session traces.

mira: will add server-side check + telemetry. ben you take console/UX + docs?

ben: on it. will add console badge + link to support flow. planning a quick changelog for enterprise customers.

Sara K: I'll open the PR with tests and repro case. tagging @infra-oncall to watch canary too.

gateway-bot: infra-oncall notified for canary watch: @infra-oncall

Dave: thanks all. let's aim to ship the fix and canary tomorrow. if infra sees any spike in misroute.rate we pause. :ok_hand:
